skill.name: frontend-aesthetics
skill.description: Guides AI coding assistants toward distinctive frontend visual design, with emphasis on typography, color, motion, backgrounds, and context-specific style.
skill.summary: Helps AI assistants create distinctive frontend aesthetics instead of generic interface patterns.
skill.author: Crossbill-Highlights

security_audit.summary: The five static findings are false positives caused by design guidance language in SKILL.md. The file contains only frontend aesthetics instructions and no code, commands, network use, filesystem access, or prompt injection attempt.

static_findings.snippet: You tend to converge toward generic, "on distribution" outputs. In frontend design,this creates what
- Typography: Choose fonts that are beautiful, unique, and interesting. Avoid generic fonts like Ari
- Backgrounds: Create atmosphere and depth rather than defaulting to solid colors. Layer CSS gradien
Interpret creatively and make unexpected choices that feel genuinely designed for the context. Vary

finding_verdicts.reason: The line critiques generic frontend output and asks for distinctive visual design. It does not request host inspection, secret access, network activity, or system reconnaissance.
The line gives typography guidance and names common fonts to avoid. This is design advice, not discovery of system details or sensitive environment data.
The line recommends visual background techniques such as gradients and geometric patterns. It has no instruction to inspect the runtime system or collect host information.
The line is a section heading about avoiding generic AI-generated aesthetics. It contains no operational command, data access request, or prompt injection language.
The line asks for creative visual variation within frontend design work. It does not ask the assistant to enumerate files, inspect hardware, or gather system information.

content.value_statement: Many generated frontends look generic and reuse the same fonts, palettes, and layouts. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code concrete design direction for distinctive interfaces.
actual_capabilities: Recommends distinctive typography choices over common default font stacks.
Encourages cohesive color themes with CSS variables and sharp accent colors.
Guides motion design through animations, page-load reveals, and focused micro-interactions.
Suggests layered backgrounds, gradients, patterns, and contextual visual effects.
Flags common generated design patterns that make interfaces feel generic.
limitations: Does not provide component code, templates, or reusable design assets.
Does not check accessibility, contrast, or responsive behavior by itself.
Does not replace user testing or review by a professional designer.
Depends on the assistant applying the guidance during frontend work.

use_cases.title: Refresh a Product Screen
use_cases.description: Turn a plain dashboard or settings page into a more distinctive interface.

use_cases.title: Set a Visual Direction
use_cases.description: Explore typography, color, motion, and background choices for a new feature.

use_cases.title: Improve Prototype Polish
use_cases.description: Give an early demo a stronger visual identity before stakeholder review.

prompt_templates.title: Improve One Page
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a single screen.
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply the frontend-aesthetics skill to this page. Improve typography, color, spacing, background treatment, and motion while keeping the current functionality.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Feature View
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for a new interface.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a frontend design for this feature using distinctive typography, a cohesive theme, purposeful motion, and a contextual background.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Visual System
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for consistent product direction.
prompt_templates.prompt: Define a visual system for this app. Include font direction, color variables, motion principles, background style, and anti-generic design rules.

prompt_templates.title: Audit and Rework UI
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for critique and implementation guidance.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this interface for generic AI design patterns. Then rework it with specific, context-aware choices for typography, palette, layout, motion, and atmosphere.

output_examples.input: A task dashboard looks like a standard generated admin panel.
output_examples.output: The skill would recommend a distinctive heading font, a focused accent color, layered workspace backgrounds, and a restrained page-load reveal.

output_examples.input: A marketing signup page uses common purple gradients and default fonts.
output_examples.output: The skill would push for a context-specific palette, more expressive typography, sharper visual hierarchy, and fewer predictable section patterns.

output_examples.input: A React feature needs motion without making the interface feel busy.
output_examples.output: The skill would suggest one high-impact reveal sequence and limited micro-interactions tied to meaningful state changes.

best_practices: Pair the guidance with concrete product context, audience, and brand constraints.
Ask the assistant to justify typography, color, motion, and background choices.
Review final screens for accessibility, responsive behavior, and visual hierarchy.
anti_patterns: Use it as a substitute for accessibility review or usability testing.
Ask for visual variety without providing product context or target users.
Force every interface into decorative motion or unusual typography.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps AI assistants produce frontend interfaces with stronger typography, color, motion, backgrounds, and visual identity.

faq.question: Does this skill generate complete components?
faq.answer: No. It provides design direction that an assistant can apply while building or revising frontend code.

faq.question: Can Claude use this skill?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill is compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Is this only for landing pages?
faq.answer: No. It can guide dashboards, product screens, prototypes, and other frontend experiences.

faq.question: Does it cover accessibility checks?
faq.answer: No. Accessibility and contrast checks should be requested separately during implementation review.

faq.question: Does this skill execute code?
faq.answer: No. It is a prose guidance file and contains no scripts or runtime commands.
